risks.title: Third-Party Supplier Dependence
risks.score_rationale: HPE relies heavily on third-party suppliers, contract manufacturers, and single-source or limited-source suppliers. Failures in managing these relationships could materially affect financial results.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Data Protection Risks
risks.score_rationale: System security incidents, data breaches, and cyberattacks could disrupt internal operations and IT services delivered to customers, reducing revenues and damaging reputation.

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: HPE operates in a highly competitive sector with major and emerging competitors expanding integrated offerings, exerting increased competitive pressure on pricing and market share.

risks.title: Geopolitical and Trade Risks
risks.score_rationale: Tariff uncertainties, import/export restrictions, trade tensions, and global restrictive trade measures could impact operations and financial results.

risks.title: Innovation and New Product Development
risks.score_rationale: HPE must continue innovating to remain competitive amid rapid technological evolution in AI, hybrid cloud, edge computing, and data security, requiring substantial R&D investments.

risks.title: Supply Chain Constraints
risks.score_rationale: Current constraints on GPUs, accelerated processing units, and other key components, coupled with macroeconomic uncertainties, could impact production and revenues.

risks.title: Regulatory and Tax Risks
risks.score_rationale: Proposed tax reforms, implementation of the OECD Pillar Two framework with a 15% global minimum tax rate, and IRS audits could increase tax complexity and expenses.

ai_positioning.summary: HPE integrates AI into its product and service offerings, particularly within its hybrid cloud solutions, servers, and networking infrastructure. The company is building AI-For-Networks and AI-For-Compute solutions, while leveraging AI to enhance internal operations and data analytics.
